Sa'vak held fast. He and Saoirse had been dispatched, to recover a stolen Royal. Sa'vak could feel the haste in Aluth, driven hard by Saoirse. They had found the ambush sight, and Aluth had found a scent. The monster cut the ocean, with its giant body, flying through the water. He was bigger, Aluth. It was a strange phenomenon, something that would need to be investigated.

Aluth began to circle, his tongue, tasting the water. Slowly his circle began to tighten, as the beast began to sink. On the bottom, they found pits. Old slave pits, by the look of them. Dark and foreboding, a warren to die in. Saoirse turned to Sa'vak and said, "I will hold Aluth here, do you think you can manage"? Sa'vak turned to her, and said "I will manage, if I die, then I am weak". With that, Sa'vak swam down to the entrance. He entered the cave, swimming on the top, his spears at the ready.

Ten metres in from the entrance, he saw tiny bubbles. Slowly he centred himself above them, then kicked off the cave roof, diving down. Head first he went, driving his spears into the necks of two guards. They never saw their death coming, he summersaulted at the bottom of his dive, and pushed off the cave floor. He rose back up, and continued on, along the cave roof. Twice more, he ended the lives of those within, culling the weak. Until at last, he came to a large chamber. Sitting on a throne, was a retched looking Lot'dy, a self proclaimed king.

Sa'vak entered the chamber, and approached the pretender. "I have come for the child, give it to me, and you may yet flee, before the Legion arrives".

"It's dead." Nor'vak got up off the throne. He threw a sack towards Sa'vak. It rolled toward his feet, revealing a dead Naga. "Shame. It wasn't me, Tempest killed it."

He cracked his neck, the faint noise echoing in the silence in the cave. "But you are here now."

The death of a Naga Royal at the hands of a Lot'dy. Even the Ha'lot'dy would feel the ramifications. His own people would suffer for this, a rage began to enter Sa'vak. The thirst for battle rose in him.

"I will kill you for this, for everyone one of my people who will suffer, I will Kill you"!

Sa'vak charged, a spear in either hand, darting forward, he slashed at the child killers neck!

As if it was premonition, this sight and focus made Nor'vak see where the blow would land. He quickly parried it, faster reflexes then he had before. But his injuries were still fresh, he was weak in comparison. He could feel the power in Sa'vaks blows. He retreated, backing up slowly. He would lead him to caves. Where the tight corridors restricted movement. Where the darkness was his advantage.

Sa'vak pressed his attack. Fighting in water was different, you had to plan three, four moves ahead. It was possible to see your death coming, and be unable to move, your body caught in a viscous prison. So Sa'vak jabbed, thinking offensively, and defensively, and the King retreated. Into a dark cavern they went, Sa'vak intent on only one thing, the death of this monster.

The darkness surrounded them, they were soon fighting in pitch black. Sa'vak heard the clink of his spear against rock. His opponent was no longer in front of him.

Nor'vak managed to dodge the last attack barely, holding his breath he silently moved away. There was no match for how silent he could be, even to slow his heartbeat so that he could hear the heartbeat of his opponent. But now he couldn't hear it, he heard instead the gnashing of teeth, growing louder. "OUT OF MY HEAD EELS" he screamed in his head. His injuries too got worse, not every parry was perfect.

But he had managed to confuse Sa'vak enough, he silently swam around him and jabbed quickly before pulling back again into a silent orbit around him.

Sa'vak felt a sharp pain in his back, a spear had bitten him. He knew it was bad, but the jab had been blind, so it was not as deep as could have been. He pushed off the floor, and threw one his spears sideways. Hoping Nor'vak would take the bait. He summersaulted at the top of his jump, and hung on the ceiling, ready to push down.

Sa'vak stopped swimming. Now he felt the sting of his own blow.

"This will never work!" He lamented in his thoughts. "I can't kill him injuring myself like this."

He felt Sa'vaks spear whiz past him and grabbed it. Thinking quickly he swam with it silently and when it should have hit the wall he instead threw himself into it. "Urrrk!" he let out a cry and silently lodged the spear in the wall.

Then he moved off to the side. He would let Sa'vak try to investigate it.

Sa'vak heard a cry, had he hit with his diversion. Which way did throw? He was upside down, and had done a summersault. He was confused. So did the only thing he could, he threw his second spear, in the general direction of the shout, and heard it strike rock. He heard a second, dull clink, then he saw it. A little bubble, followed by another. Sa'vak drew his knife, and dived after the bubbles. Before him, loomed a head. He jabbed his knife into its neck.

Nor'vak was fooled, how easily fooled. A lucky spear's throw. He grabbed Sa'vak as he was driving the knife through his neck. He brought their heads together, then bit into Sa'vaks neck. Sa'vak responded, driving the knife deeper into Nor'vak neck, twisting it around. But the pain only fueled Nor'vaks rage. He clamped harder and harder, in his death throes he sheared Sa'vaks tissue. Sa'vak was finally able to pull back, without a throat.

Nor'vak lay pinned against the cave wall, blood had finally stopped pouring out of him as his heart stopped beating. He was left in his final moments to his thoughts. They were a resounding accomplishment. He had done it. He killed him!

The creatures in his mind rejoiced, cheering, growing louder. Then they turned nasty. They turned on him. They began to eat his mind, ripping him apart. The evil seeing its host become weak had no appreciation for it. They bit into him madly. All the voices he entertained turned on him. As his consciousness and life faded he only felt absolute and complete terror and hatred.

Sa'vak felt his throat ripped out, a gaping gash, where the monster had bitten into him. He cut into his leather greaves, and tied them around his neck. The wound at his back would have to wait, he picked up a spear, and began to hobble out. Through dark passages he hobbled, into the cavern, where the child lay. He bent, and gently lifted her corpse, leaving the spear behind, he left the cavern. A trail of blood marked his passage, as he made his way out to the entrance. Sa'vak hobbled out of the slave pits, into the light. A shadow fell over him, and Aluth swam past. The leviathan turned, and stopped. Saoirse dismounted, and approached Sa'vak. He made eye contact with her, and shook his head. She reached him, and slapped him across the face. The shame stung Sa'vak to his core. Saoirse took the child's body in her arms, and turned her back on Sa'vak. She left him there, in the shadow of the pits, his body wrecked, to die.

Sa'vak goes to retrieve the Naga infant, Nor'vak tells him that it is dead. In a fit of righteous fury, Sav'ak attacks Nor'vak, who is still heavily wounded and retrieves into the dark depths of the caverns. There, Sa'vak slays Nor'vak, but is mortally wounded in the process. He brings the dead infant to Saoirse and is left to die, only to be given a new purpose by Tempest: Befriend Mar'dy and watch over him, and kill him if he starts a new rebellion.

There is no valid reason.

It is 100% defensible to require people to prove they are a member of the group(s) allowed to vote in a given eating contest before accepting their vote and counting it in the eating contest.

If obtaining the thing that can prove this (voter ID or other acceptable ID) is not 100% free of cost and unhindered by unrelated factors (skin color, language, etc) for eligible voters, then something is wrong with the people or organizations providing the ID.

The solution is to fix the ID issuance issue, not remove the ID requirement. Most of the objections to voter ID I've seen fail to make this distinction:

It Costs or Will Cost Too Much

The process of obtaining ID that proves eligibility to vote should never cost money - even if it's a very small fee, the presence of any requirement other than proving that you're actually in the constituency implies that it's OK to create a situation where an eligible voter may be unable to vote. Nobody should support a system that operates this way.

This isn't saying "make driver's licenses" free, because those are for cars, not voting. It's OK to accept them as voter ID if a driver's license contains enough information to verify eligibility, but they are privilege licenses. There needs to be some form of ID whose primary purpose is identifying eligibility to vote, and it is this ID that ought to have no cost barriers.

Yes, this may cost a bit more and entail a bit more work for the governing body. Boo-hoo; serve your people.

It Will Be Too Hard

Given that it should be possible to obtain an ID that proves eligibility to vote with no cost barriers, what is hard about that? You can't go to a place to get the ID? How were you going to vote, then?

Or did you mean filling out forms was too hard? That's probably what you'll have to do to actually cast your vote, you know.

To ensure that anyone who is eligible to vote and actually chooses to attempt to vote is not disenfranchised, every means of accepting votes should also have the capacity to validate eligibility to vote.

Polling locations should have a physical place to prove eligibility to vote at that location (even if they can't issue a physical ID card on-the-spot). Does an election accept ballots by mail? They should also permit obtaining valid voter ID by mail. Does an election permit online voting? Then they should also be able to issue voter IDs online.

With this, there is no excuse around the difficulty of proving eligibility to vote - if you are willing and able to vote, then your vote can be counted.

Yes, this is a bit more work for the governing body. Boo-hoo; serve your people.

Some Eligible Voters Won't Be Able to Prove Eligibility to Vote

This is an instance of the logical fallacy of "Begging the Question" - if someone can't prove they're eligible to vote, then they are not actually an "eligible voter."

This is the whole point of voter ID - so that people who, by the laws of the land, cannot demonstrate that they are eligible to vote don't get to cast votes.

Will there be some people who probably actually are eligible to vote but can't prove it, whose votes have been being accepted for a long time but now that elections start doing due-diligence, won't have their votes accepted? Probably.

This doesn't change the fact that such people literally cannot prove they are eligible to vote. It is neither fair nor consistent to accept their votes but not other ineligible voters' votes. It is an instance of the nirvana fallacy to reject moving to validating eligibility to vote from not validating eligibility to vote out of fear that it won't be perfect from day 1.

If case studies like the "probably" link above truly upset people, then the laws governing proving eligibility need to be fixed. The solution is not to continue to accept all votes without validating that they came from someone eligible to vote.

IDs Will Be Witheld From [Demographic] to Disenfranchise Them
